bullets.text: Halvern Dam on the Sorrel River above Brindlemark in the Assek Valley was reported damaged on 9 September 2025, with the damage extending to the dam's right abutment.
The damage prompted a dam safety emergency in which the alert level for the valley was raised from Yellow to Orange within a day of the first reports.
No casualties were reported in the window; roughly 11,800 residents were moved out of Brindlemark under a mandatory evacuation, with Ferris Hollow also evacuated.
The Sorrel Basin Water Authority provided information on the dam's condition, and the evacuation was still under way at the end of the window with the cause of the damage not yet stated.
Damage to Halvern Dam and its right abutment is reported on the afternoon of the first day.
The Sorrel Basin Water Authority provides information on the dam within minutes of the first damage reports.
A mandatory evacuation is ordered for Brindlemark and Ferris Hollow the following morning; the alert level is raised from Yellow to Orange.
Roughly 11,800 residents move out of Brindlemark as the evacuation proceeds toward the end of the window.
Halvern Dam and its right abutment were damaged.
A mandatory evacuation was ordered for Brindlemark after the dam was damaged.
Residents of Ferris Hollow were also evacuated under the same order.
Roughly 11,800 residents were moved out of Brindlemark under the mandatory evacuation.
